rule: Laws enacted in the 2021, 2021A, 2021B, 2022 and 2022C sessions whose final staff analysis names a kind of business it helps, as screened by the Senate slice; House floor votes of Nixon and Chambliss.

bills.title: Farming Operations

benefits.quote: This bill may reduce litigation costs faced by farms based on nuisance lawsuits.

bills.screen: This bill may reduce litigation costs faced by farms based on nuisance lawsuits. On the other hand, persons adversely affected by a farm operation will have more difficulties in obtaining redress. At least in some cases, plaintiffs will need to prove that the farm operation was in violation of environmental laws.

bills.title: Construction Contracting Regulation Exemption

benefits.category: Seminole and Miccosukee tribal chickee builders (construction without a contractor license)
benefits.quote: The bill may have a positive impact on the private sector by allowing members of the Seminole Tribe of Florida and the Miccosukee Tribe of Indians of Florida to construct chickees

bills.screen: The bill may have a positive impact on the private sector by allowing members of the Seminole Tribe of Florida and the Miccosukee Tribe of Indians of Florida to construct chickees without having to obtain a license or work for a licensed contractor.
bills.note: judgment call: beneficiaries are tribal members who build chickees as a trade

bills.title: Broadband Internet Infrastructure

benefits.quote: Broadband Internet providers will benefit from significantly discounted rates for certain attachments made to municipal electric utility poles

bills.screen: Broadband Internet providers will benefit from significantly discounted rates for certain attachments made to municipal electric utility poles over the next three years and from the certainty that any non- discounted rates applicable to other attachments on these poles may not be increased for 13 months. These savings, together with the potential award of grants, should provide incentives for additional investment in broadband Internet infrastructure to reach unserved areas and unserved customers in this state. This may result in increased economic activity in areas that currently lack access to broadband Internet service.

bills.title: Taxation

benefits.category: owners of affordable multifamily housing; businesses using Strong Families / Internship tax credits
benefits.quote: Owners of multifamily projects that provide housing to extremely-low-income, very-low-income, or low- income families ... will realize additional savings on ad valorem taxes.

bills.screen: Owners of multifamily projects that provide housing to extremely-low-income, very-low-income, or low- income families, and educational institutions that meet the new exemption parameters for leases, will realize additional savings on ad valorem taxes. Business making contributions to eligible charitable organizations under the Strong Families Tax Credit, or who employ student interns under the Internship Tax Credit, will benefit from the dollar-for-dollar credit against certain tax liabilities. The Back-To-School, Disaster Preparedness, and Freedom Week sales tax holidays will provide tax relief to Florida consumers.

bills.title: Liability of Persons Providing Areas for Public Outdoor Recreational Purposes

benefits.category: private landowners operating outdoor recreation areas with concessions or special events
benefits.quote: This may result in an indeterminate, positive fiscal impact on private property owners that derive such revenue and retain the liability protection.

bills.screen: CS/CS/SB 920 expands liability protections to include “traversing or crossing for the purpose of ingress and egress to and from, and access to and from, public lands or lands owned or leased by a state agency which are used for outdoor recreational purposes.” This additional liability protection may encourage private property owners to make areas available to the public for outdoor recreational purposes. The bill creates an exception where an owner of an area used for outdoor recreational purposes may derive revenue from concessions or special events and retain liability protection if such revenue is used exclusively to maintain, manage, and improve the outdoor recreational area. This may result in an indeterminate, positive fiscal impact on private property owners that derive such revenue and retain the liability protection. BILL: CS/CS/SB 920 Page 5

bills.title: Largemouth Bass

benefits.category: aquaculture producers and dealers (Florida largemouth bass)
benefits.quote: Certified aquaculture producers and dealers with a nonrecreational license from FWC could see a financial benefit

bills.screen: Certified aquaculture producers and dealers with a nonrecreational license from FWC could see a financial benefit from the ability to offer Florida largemouth bass for sale.

bills.title: Medicaid

benefits.quote: The bill will increase reimbursements paid to ambulance providers

bills.screen: The bill will increase reimbursements paid to ambulance providers that provide non- emergency transportation to dually-eligible individuals.

bills.title: Credit for Reinsurance

benefits.category: domestic insurers and reinsurers in reciprocal jurisdictions
benefits.quote: provides U.S. domestic insurers with greater access to global reinsurance

bills.screen: Allowing insurers to receive credit for reinsurance and eliminating additional collateral requirements for reinsurers if the reinsurer is domiciled in a “reciprocal jurisdiction” provides U.S. domestic insurers with greater access to global reinsurance and improves diversification of risk. 40 See s. 624.610(3)(e), F.S. BILL: SB 728 Page 10

bills.title: Child Support

benefits.category: financial institutions in the FAST Levy program; parenting-course providers
benefits.quote: Financial institutions that participate in the Federally Assisted State Transmitted (FAST) Levy program may experience cost savings

bills.screen: Private businesses will need to start reporting independent contractors’ information to the State Directory of New Hires and the new reporting requirement may require more resources and additional costs to private businesses. Incarcerated parents will benefit from not having their incarceration treated as voluntary unemployment, as income will not be imputed to them while they have no ability to pay, reducing the amount in past-due child support they would otherwise owe. Financial institutions that participate in the Federally Assisted State Transmitted (FAST) Levy program may experience cost savings with the improved efficiencies associated with participating in the program such as processing levy notices from multiple states in a standardized, automated manner. Providers of parenting courses that address children having special needs or emotional concerns may experience greater demands for their courses and greater revenues.
bills.note: mixed: also new reporting cost on businesses

bills.title: Alarm System Contractors

benefits.quote: The bill may have a positive impact on the private sector by allowing electrical and alarm system contractors to begin repairs on fire alarm systems without having to wait to obtain a permit

bills.screen: The bill may have a positive impact on the private sector by allowing electrical and alarm system contractors to begin repairs on fire alarm systems without having to wait to obtain a permit, and allowing companies to advertise in multiple states using the same advertisement.

bills.title: Fire Sprinklers

benefits.quote: The authorization to do this type of work is expanded for persons certified as a Contractor I or Contractor II

bills.screen: The bill authorizes persons certified as a Contractor I or Contractor II to design the alteration of an existing system regardless of the size of the system, if the alteration relocates or delete 249 or fewer sprinklers. The authorization to do this type of work is expanded for persons certified as a Contractor I or Contractor II, which may impact others who have previously undertaken such design work, such as engineers and architects. Under the bill, persons certified as a Contractor V may contract for work involving the inspection, alteration, repair, and servicing of underground piping for a fire protection system only if they are under the direction of persons certified as a Contractor I or Contractor II. The requirement imposed by the bill may result in decreased opportunities for work for a Contractor V. BILL: CS/SB 286 Page 7

bills.title: Payment for Construction Services

benefits.quote: a positive fiscal impact for subcontractors and parties lower in the chain of contracts

bills.screen: The increased interest rates applied to unpaid contractual obligations for construction labor, services, and materials may have a negative fiscal impact for prime contractors and a positive fiscal impact for subcontractors and parties lower in the chain of contracts.

bills.title: Waste Management

benefits.category: private solid waste collection companies (displaced franchise haulers)
benefits.quote: There may be an indeterminate, positive economic impact on the private sector because ... the displaced companies are assured three years' notice

bills.screen: There may be an indeterminate, positive economic impact on the private sector because the bill deletes the authorization in current law for local governments to pay the displaced company 15 months of gross receipts instead of providing three year’s notice so that the displaced companies are assured three years’ notice prior to displacement and 18 months of gross receipts when their service ends.

bills.title: Department of Business and Professional Regulation

benefits.category: construction and electrical contractors; small cosmetic manufacturers
benefits.quote: construction and electrical contractors would not have to pay the $4 fee ... opportunity for small cosmetic manufacturing businesses

bills.screen: The bill has an indeterminate positive fiscal impact for the private sector. Under the bill, construction and electrical contractors would not have to pay the $4 fee to the Department of Business and Professional Regulation (DBPR) at the time of application or 104 See Department of Business and Professional Regulation, CS/SB 1966 Bill Analysis, p. 10, (Apr. 1, 2021) (on file with the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Agriculture, Environment, and General Government). BILL: CS/CS/SB 1966 Page 22 renewal to fund projects relating to the building construction industry or continuing education programs. The bill may provide an opportunity for small cosmetic manufacturing businesses to generate revenues up to $25,000 in annual gross sales without the cost of a cosmetic manufacturing permit. Relating to cosmetic manufacturers, the bill may save license expenses needed to continue operation of the business during permitting transfers due to change of ownership, change of controlling interest, or change of location. According to the DBPR, the bill will eliminate the dual permit fee many firms currently pay to continue operating pending approval of the new permit.105

bills.title: Podiatric Medicine

benefits.category: podiatric physicians (direct health care agreements); continuing-education providers
benefits.quote: Podiatric physicians may establish direct health care agreements without concern of facing regulatory action

bills.screen: Organizations currently authorized to offer the continuing education course on controlled substances prescribing may experience a loss in revenue due to increased competition, since additional organizations may be eligible to provide the course. Podiatric physicians may establish direct health care agreements without concern of facing regulatory action, which may increase access to podiatric care.

bills.title: Scheduling of Drug Products Containing Cannabidiol

benefits.quote: Descheduling Epidiolex allows doctors and pharmacies to prescribe and dispense the drug without having to comply with burdensome regulations

bills.screen: Descheduling Epidiolex allows doctors and pharmacies to prescribe and dispense the drug without having to comply with burdensome regulations and reporting requirements.

bills.title: Postsecondary Education

benefits.quote: CS/CS/SB 52 may reduce expenses for private schools no longer required to pay costs associated with dual enrollment students

bills.screen: CS/CS/SB 52 may reduce expenses for private schools no longer required to pay costs associated with dual enrollment students. The financial supports for dual enrollment courses may increase opportunities for Florida secondary students to take college-credit courses that will count toward an associate or baccalaureate degree while still in high school, which may reduce costs for students and families.

bills.title: Craft Distilleries

benefits.quote: The bill may increase total sales revenue for craft distilleries

bills.screen: The bill may increase total sales revenue for craft distilleries by 1) allowing craft distilleries to sell their branded products to consumers by the drink and by 2) repealing the six individual container limit on sales of each of the craft distillery’s branded products to a consumer at a craft distillery’s souvenir gift shop. The bill would provide additional sources of revenue for craft distilleries located in a community redevelopment area that qualify for a vendor’s license, as specified in the bill. BILL: CS/CS/SB 46 Page 10

bills.title: Public Works

benefits.category: public-works contractors, subcontractors and material suppliers
benefits.quote: to the extent more contractors, subcontractors, or material suppliers or carriers would no longer be required to meet certain pre-bid requirements

bills.screen: The bill may have a positive indeterminate impact to the extent more contractors, subcontractors, or material suppliers or carriers would no longer be required to meet certain pre-bid requirements.

bills.title: Recovery of Spaceflight Assets

benefits.quote: The bill safeguards the property rights of spaceflight entities to spaceflight assets

bills.screen: The bill may have a positive fiscal impact on the private sector. The bill safeguards the property rights of spaceflight entities to spaceflight assets, ensuring the owner of the spaceflight asset can recover the asset to reuse it in future missions.

bills.title: Florida Building Code

benefits.quote: Prohibiting local governments from requiring contracts between owners and builders ... may have a positive impact

bills.screen: Prohibiting certain building design elements ordinances and other regulations may lead to a decrease in the cost of construction. Prohibiting local governments from requiring contracts between owners and builders as a condition to apply or obtain a building permit may have a positive impact by preventing certain proprietary information from becoming public.

bills.title: Home-based Businesses

benefits.quote: The bill may allow more home-based businesses to operate more freely and efficiently.

bills.screen: The bill may allow more home-based businesses to operate more freely and efficiently.

bills.title: Growth Management

benefits.quote: The bill may reduce development costs for landowners

bills.screen: The bill may reduce development costs for landowners that determine developing property under the comprehensive plan and land development regulations of a new municipality are more advantageous than continuing under a preexisting development order.

bills.title: Barber Services

benefits.quote: This will provide barbers with more flexibility to offer their customers more services outside a barbershop.

bills.screen: The bill will allow barbers to practice shampooing, hair cutting, or hair arranging without needing to perform such services in a barbershop or to make appointments for such services through a barbershop, which will bring them in line with current cosmetology requirements. This will provide barbers with more flexibility to offer their customers more services outside a barbershop.

bills.title: Implementation of the 2021 Gaming Compact Between the Seminole Tribe of Florida and the State of Florida

benefits.quote: Licensed pari-mutuel facilities ... will receive revenue for such services.

bills.screen: Licensed pari-mutuel facilities, if eligible to be qualified pari-mutuel permitholders providing marketing and similar services to the Seminole Tribe, will receive revenue for such services. BILL: CS/SB 2-A Page 21

bills.title: COVID-19-related Claims Against Health Care Providers

benefits.quote: the bill will have a positive fiscal impact on the health care industry

bills.screen: The private sector fiscal impacts of SPB 7014 are indeterminate. If the effect of the bill is to codify what the courts would have found to be the common law of the state, then the bill will have a significant positive impact on the private sector in general through the 2 Section 768.381(6), F.S. BILL: SB 7014 Page 3 avoidance of litigation and its attendant costs. If the effect of the bill is to limit lawsuits that otherwise would have yielded recoveries for injured parties, the bill will have a positive fiscal impact on the health care industry and a corresponding negative fiscal impact on injured individuals.

bills.title: Acute and Post-acute Hospital Care at Home

benefits.quote: By allowing private hospitals to serve patients at their homes ... may allow health care services to be provided in a more cost effective manner

bills.screen: By allowing private hospitals to serve patients at their homes through the use of paramedics and hospital pharmacies, CS/CS/SB 1222 may allow health care services to be provided in a more cost effective manner. Moreover, the ability to treat a hospital patient at his or her home may make additional hospital beds available for patients having more serious conditions.

bills.title: Patient Care in Health Care Facilities

benefits.category: home health agencies and ALS ambulance services
benefits.quote: which could have a positive, but indeterminate, fiscal impact on these providers

bills.screen: The bill creates staffing efficiencies for home health agencies and ALS ambulance services, which could have a positive, but indeterminate, fiscal impact on these providers.

bills.title: Nursing Homes

benefits.quote: The bill may have a positive fiscal impact on nursing homes resulting from the reduction in the number of hours of required CNA direct care

bills.screen: The bill may have a positive fiscal impact on nursing homes resulting from the reduction in the number of hours of required CNA direct care from 2.5 hours to 2 hours per resident per day. The bill may have a negative fiscal impact on nursing homes due to an increase in litigation costs related to the inadmissibility of evidence of compliance with state minimum staffing requirements as evidence of compliance with federal staffing requirements. The bill may have a positive fiscal impact on claimants with unsatisfied judgments against nursing homes as the bill enhances their opportunity to recoup such judgments.

bills.title: Procedures for Petitions for Utility Rate Relief

benefits.category: investor-owned electric utilities (Florida Public Utilities Company)
benefits.quote: The bill may have a positive fiscal impact on public electric utilities that become eligible to utilize the proposed agency action procedure for rate relief

bills.screen: The bill may have a positive fiscal impact on public electric utilities that become eligible to utilize the proposed agency action procedure for rate relief in lieu of a standard rate case. This may minimize litigation and regulatory costs. These cost avoidances may result in savings, or prevent increases, to the ratepayers. It appears the Florida Public Utilities Company’s Electric Division will be eligible to utilize the PAA procedure for rate relief due to its annual sale level. The bill does not affect natural gas utilities regulated by the PSC as they do not have a statutory annual sales threshold to qualify for the PAA procedure. 36 Id. BILL: SB 350 Page 6

bills.title: Swimming Pool Specialty Contracting Services

benefits.quote: An unlimited number of unlicensed persons may be supervised by a contractor licensed to construct ... swimming pools

bills.screen: Persons who are not licensed as contractors in a trade and have not been eligible to engage in such work may now, under the supervision of certified or registered contractors whose licenses cover such work, construct, remodel, repair, or improve swimming pools, interactive water features, hot tubs, or spas. An unlimited number of unlicensed persons may be supervised by a contractor licensed to construct, remodel, repair, or improve swimming pools, interactive water features, hot tubs, or spas, although the contractor is responsible for the work that is performed. This may increase the availability of work for those who are not licensed, or in the process of becoming licensed.

bills.title: Trusts

benefits.quote: could lower the costs that these entities incur while operating in Florida

bills.screen: SB 1368 appears to simplify trust administration relating to family trust companies, licensed family trust companies, or foreign licensed family trust companies and thus could lower the costs that these entities incur while operating in Florida. In addition, the extending of the allowable life of trusts in Florida may encourage more trusts to be established in the state.

bills.title: Private Provider Inspections of Onsite Sewage Treatment and Disposal Systems

benefits.quote: Private sector businesses that can serve the functions provided for in the bill may see a positive fiscal impact

bills.screen: Private sector businesses that can serve the functions provided for in the bill may see a positive fiscal impact from the bill.

bills.title: Money Services Businesses

benefits.quote: the regulatory clarity provided by the bill may result in such businesses foregoing licensure

bills.screen: The bill’s overall impact on the private sector, while likely positive, is indeterminate. The bill provides regulatory clarity as to the way in which virtual currency is regulated under ch. 560, F.S. To the extent that the Espinoza case may have caused some businesses to become licensed out of an abundance of caution when buying and selling virtual currency in two-party transactions, the regulatory clarity STORAGE NAME: h0273z1.DOCX PAGE: 9 DATE: 5/13/2022 provided by the bill may result in such businesses foregoing licensure. Additionally, the bill may lead to greater protection for consumers transacting in virtual currency through third-party intermediaries. The regulatory clarity provided by the bill may lead to more money transmitter licensees, especially those that deal in virtual currency. Businesses that apply for a money transmitter license would be subject to fees for initial licensure ($375), biannual renewal ($750), fingerprinting of control persons (approximately $65 per individual for initial fingerprinting plus $6 per individual biannually for fingerprint retention), and examination expenses every 5 years (approximately $3,800). 83

bills.title: School Concurrency

benefits.quote: Private sector development may benefit to the extent that the bill streamlines school concurrency requirements

bills.screen: Private sector development may benefit to the extent that the bill streamlines school concurrency requirements. BILL: CS/CS/CS/SB 706 Page 5

bills.title: Alarm Systems

benefits.category: fire alarm system contractors and agents
benefits.quote: the expedited permitting process for fire alarm system alterations may reduce the time and cost

bills.screen: According to the Department of Business and Professional Regulation (DBPR), the expenditures will be reduced for initial training and continuing education by applicants and licensees (with the required certifications) who seek or renew a fire alarm system agent license.56 Further, the expedited permitting process for fire alarm system alterations may reduce the time and cost involved for such permits.57

bills.title: Consumer Finance Loans

benefits.quote: This may allow companies with less liquid assets to become licensed as a consumer finance lender.

bills.screen: This may allow companies with less liquid assets to become licensed as a consumer finance lender.

bills.title: Department of Financial Services

benefits.category: construction-industry small businesses; workers' compensation insurers
benefits.quote: should reduce the cost of non-compliance for small businesses, particularly those in the construction industry

bills.screen: Reducing the penalty calculation period and increasing credits for businesses that fail to comply with the workers’ compensation law, so long as the business has not previously failed to provide workers’ compensation coverage for its employees, should reduce the cost of non-compliance for small businesses, particularly those in the construction industry. Permitting payroll audits by mail, rather than in person, for employers in the construction industry that have an estimated annual workers’ compensation premium of less than $10,000 could result in modest cost savings for insurance carriers. Permitting unaffiliated insurance agents to adjust claims, so long as the agent is also a licensed adjuster, could create employment opportunities for persons who hold both licenses and increase the pool of adjusters who can respond in the aftermath of a large storm or catastrophic event. Terminating the Florida Patient’s Compensation Fund could result in refunds to doctors and hospitals that were members of the Fund in the late 1970s and early 1980s.

bills.title: Insolvent Insurers

benefits.quote: The bill provides flexibility to insurance carriers by providing the option of paying assessments on an annual or quarterly basis.

bills.screen: The bill provides flexibility to insurance carriers by providing the option of paying assessments on an annual or quarterly basis. Insurance carriers would not be required to recoup the cost of an assessment if, for example, the administrative cost of recoupment outweighs the benefit of recoupment.

bills.title: Residential Development Projects for Affordable Housing

benefits.quote: Developers incorporating affordable housing into development projects may benefit

bills.screen: Developers incorporating affordable housing into development projects may benefit from bypassing comprehensive plan amendments and other delays in project approval.
